reason: The hypothesis directly mirrors the findings of E1, which reports the exact microstructure, mechanism, and quantitative outcomes (~35% elongation, ~2 GPa) for a phase-selectively recrystallized EHEA. E2 provides general context on eutectic alloy brittleness but does not independently support the specific intervention or outcomes. All key premises are accurately represented and supported by E1.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization can fully recrystallize the soft fcc phase while retaining a continuous hard B2 phase skeleton in EHEAs.
This microstructure eliminates weak boundaries and fully releases strain hardening capacity of both phases.
The resulting microstructure improves strain partitioning, delaying crack initiation.
The treatment achieves ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress in an EHEA.
The concept is applicable to various duplex alloys with soft and hard phases.
